title: Note The Difference Between The 1st Chapter And The 2nd Chapter

questions.question: Who is the main figure mentioned in this passage, and what mission is he on?
questions.answer: He is a traveler sent into the world to reach faith, and he is searching for his Creator with certainty.

questions.question: How did this traveler carry out his search before this new stage began?
questions.answer: He examined the whole universe in his mind and asked created things about their Maker.

questions.question: What had he already reached with full conviction before starting this new journey?
questions.answer: He had reached certainty that his Creator necessarily exists.

questions.question: What did the traveler say to his intellect at the start of the new journey?
questions.answer: He invited his intellect to join him in a fresh journey to observe proofs that Allah is One.

questions.question: What is the main subject of this chapter?
questions.answer: It is about evidences for Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: At the first stopping-place, how many major truths did they see?
questions.answer: They saw four sacred truths.

questions.question: What was special about those four truths in relation to the whole universe?
questions.answer: They were seen as ruling over the entire cosmos.

questions.question: What conclusion did those truths clearly require?
questions.answer: They clearly required the unity of Allah.

questions.question: Why is the traveler’s new journey different from his earlier one?
questions.answer: The earlier journey focused on finding the Creator’s necessary existence, while this one focuses on recognizing His unity.

questions.question: What title is given to this section of the work?
questions.answer: It is a chapter about proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: Why had the traveler been sent to the world, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He had been sent to gain faith.

questions.question: What does the traveler look for in every place?
questions.answer: He looks for his Lord and seeks to find Allah everywhere through the signs of creation.

questions.question: What does the phrase about traveling through the whole cosmos “in his mind” show?
questions.answer: It shows that his journey is mainly one of thought, reflection, and understanding.

questions.question: What certainty had the traveler already achieved?
questions.answer: He had become certain of the existence of his Creator.

questions.question: What was the purpose of beginning a new journey after reaching that certainty?
questions.answer: It was to see the evidences that prove the Creator is absolutely One.

questions.question: Who joined the traveler in this new stage?
questions.answer: His intellect joined him.

questions.question: What did they discover at the first stop of the journey?
questions.answer: They found four holy truths spread across the universe.

questions.question: How strongly does the passage present the link between those truths and Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: It presents the link as obvious and unavoidable.

questions.question: What kind of person is the traveler presented as being?
questions.answer: He is presented as a sincere seeker trying to reach true faith.

questions.question: What name is used for the Creator in a way that highlights certainty of existence?
questions.answer: The Creator is described as the Necessarily Existent One.

questions.question: After reaching certainty about existence, what issue becomes the focus of the next journey?
questions.answer: The next focus is proving Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Why is it meaningful that the traveler speaks to his intellect?
questions.answer: It shows that reason has an important role in understanding faith.

questions.question: What happened when the traveler and his intellect set out together?
questions.answer: They arrived at the first stopping-place and witnessed four sacred truths across the cosmos.

questions.question: What does the passage say those truths do by themselves?
questions.answer: It says they plainly require belief in Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Does the passage describe these truths as local and limited, or universal and wide-reaching?
questions.answer: It describes them as universal and spread over the whole cosmos.

questions.question: What relationship between belief in Allah’s existence and belief in His unity is implied here?
questions.answer: It implies that after recognizing Allah exists, a person should go on to recognize that He is One without partner.

questions.question: What is being investigated in the new journey mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The new journey investigates the signs that prove Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What was the traveler’s original goal in being in the world?
questions.answer: His original goal was to attain faith.

questions.question: How broad was the scope of his earlier search?
questions.answer: It was as broad as the whole universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say he asked all things about?
questions.answer: He asked them about their Creator.

questions.question: What result did he reach concerning his Creator before this chapter began?
questions.answer: He reached complete certainty that his Creator necessarily exists.

questions.question: What does the phrase “they set out together” refer to?
questions.answer: It refers to the traveler and his intellect beginning the new stage side by side.

questions.question: Where did they first stop in this new stage?
questions.answer: They first stopped at a place where four sacred truths were seen across the cosmos.

questions.question: What effect did those four truths have on the question of Divine unity?
questions.answer: They served as clear evidence making Divine unity necessary.

questions.question: In this passage, what kind of journey is being described more than a physical trip?
questions.answer: It is mainly an intellectual and spiritual journey.

questions.question: What had the traveler been trying to find everywhere?
questions.answer: He had been trying to find his Allah through the signs present in every place.

questions.question: What new aim did he announce to his intellect?
questions.answer: He announced that they should begin a new search for the proofs of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What was present over the entire cosmos at the first stopping-place?
questions.answer: Four sacred truths were present over the entire cosmos.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the connection between these truths and Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: It describes them as clearly and unmistakably pointing to His unity.

questions.question: What does this passage suggest about studying creation?
questions.answer: It suggests that studying creation can lead a person to stronger belief in Allah.

questions.question: What is the formal topic named at the beginning of the marked passage?
questions.answer: The topic is proofs of the unity of Allah.

questions.question: How is the traveler described in relation to faith?
questions.answer: He is described as someone sent to the world in order to gain faith.

questions.question: What method did he use to investigate the universe?
questions.answer: He mentally journeyed through it and examined what everything could show about the Creator.

questions.question: What was he seeking in every place?
questions.answer: He was seeking his Sustainer and trying to find Allah.

questions.question: What had he already established with certainty?
questions.answer: He had established the necessary existence of his Creator.

questions.question: What was the next step after that realization?
questions.answer: The next step was to look for the evidences of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: To whom did the traveler speak before beginning that next step?
questions.answer: He spoke to his intellect.

questions.question: What did the traveler and his intellect witness at the first stopping-place?
questions.answer: They witnessed four sacred truths spread throughout the cosmos.

questions.question: What made those truths important?
questions.answer: They clearly demanded the conclusion that Allah is One.
